why: Post-order combine of two facts at once: each subtree reports its height, and the node checks that its children's heights differ by at most one. Checking heights top-down instead recomputes them and costs O(n^2).
hints: Being balanced is a condition at every node. What does a node need from its two children to check it?
Compute heights bottom-up; at each node, if |hl - hr| > 1 the tree is unbalanced. Return the height upward so the parent does not recompute it.
Return -1 as an 'already unbalanced' signal so the whole recursion stops early, or use an explicit post-order stack. O(n) time.
pitfalls: Checking only the root's two subtrees is not enough; every node must satisfy the rule.
Calling a separate height() function at every node is O(n^2) on a chain.
